palette.$description: Raw color ramps. Named `palette.*` (not `color.*`) deliberately: it keeps the raw CSS variable (--palette-cedar-500) distinct from the Tailwind-facing theme key (--color-cedar-500) that globals.css maps it to, so @theme inline never has to reference a variable by its own name. Values below are calibrated to Cedar Grove LLP's actual mark (sampled from the live wordmark: ink #585947 on ivory #ecede7 — see docs/foundations/colors.mdx §"Where these numbers came from") rather than invented from scratch. This is the working default for RECOMMENDATION A ("Heritage") of three documented options — see the Foundations/Colors doc for the full comparison and how to switch.

cedar.$description: Primary brand color — the firm's actual muted olive/moss (hue ~64°), not a generic "cedar tree" green. cedar-700 (#5c5d4b) is essentially the real logo ink color.

clay.$description: Secondary accent. Warm tan/terracotta, muted to sit quietly alongside cedar rather than compete with it — used sparingly for highlights, chart categories, and editorial accents. Never as the primary action color.

neutral.$description: Warm-leaning gray scale, hue-matched to the real ivory background (#ecede7) rather than a cold blue-gray — used for text, surfaces, and borders. Also serves as the base for RECOMMENDATION B ("Ink-first"): neutral-900/950 as the primary action color instead of cedar, see the Foundations/Colors doc.

color.$description: Status/utility colors, consumed only by alias (tokens/semantic/*.json) rather than exposed as direct utility classes — they never appear on the left-hand side of a @theme mapping, so no naming collision risk applies to this group.

success.$description: Status color: positive/complete states. Distinct hue from the cedar brand color so brand and status meaning never collide.
